justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Video Consultation Service handles consultations (R-01), Integration Service routes e-prescriptions (R-02), AI Symptom Checker predicts urgency (R-03), and Consent & Privacy Manager controls purpose-based sharing (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Bandwidth Adaptation Component and Mediasoup SFU dynamic downscaling handle low bitrates efficiently. Asynchronous Google Cloud Pub/Sub, Protobuf serialization, and local client caching (SQLite/Hive) optimize throughput and resource utilization.
justifications.compatibility: Explicitly addresses R-08 via the US Pharmacy Adapter Component supporting HL7 FHIR and the EU Gateway Adapter Component supporting EU national standards over secure mTLS, alongside Regional Identity Provider integration.
justifications.usability: Web & Mobile Client Apps serve both Patients and Clinicians with localized UI Layers and offline support, though specific clinical UI workflows and accessibility features are not detailed.
justifications.reliability: R-06 is directly satisfied by the Bandwidth Adaptation Component maintaining consultations below 300 kbit/s. Resilience is reinforced by Dead Letter Queues, Envoy circuit breaking, and multi-region GKE clusters.
justifications.security: Strong regional data residency via separate Cloud SQL instances, VPC Service Controls, and region-isolated Cloud KMS keys. Immutable Cloud Storage Bucket Lock satisfies MDR traceability (R-07), backed by mTLS and token-embedded consent.
justifications.maintainability: High modularity with decoupled microservices (Core, Video, AI, Integration). Domain logic is cleanly separated, adapters isolate external variations, and ArgoCD enables consistent regional GitOps delivery.
justifications.portability: Workloads are containerized for GKE across target regions europe-west3 and us-central1. Cross-platform client apps (Flutter/React Native) and standard container runtimes ensure environment independence.

PERF-01.justification: Mediasoup SFU and GKE regional clusters support WebRTC media routing and simulcast. However, dynamic horizontal scaling and cross-SFU pipe transports during sudden peak join bursts on GCE are not explicitly detailed, posing a minor scaling risk.
sensitivity_points: SFU auto-scaling speed and signaling connection capacity under sudden connection spikes
tradeoffs: Media server CPU utilization versus rapid WebRTC media negotiation latency

PERF-02.justification: A peak load of 50,000 requests per hour is approximately 14 requests per second. The containerized FastAPI inference engine and GKE cluster can easily handle this volume within sub-second latencies.
sensitivity_points: Batching latency and GPU/CPU inference throughput in PyTorch
tradeoffs: Model complexity versus inference response latency under peak load

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture explicitly incorporates an adaptive WebRTC client wrapper, bandwidth adaptation downscaling below 300 kbit/s, and a local encrypted storage manager on the client to avoid dropped sessions and note loss.
sensitivity_points: Accurate real-time WebRTC telemetry feedback loops for dynamic bitrate stepping
tradeoffs: Degrading video resolution to prioritize continuous audio and operational state synchronization

AVAIL-02.justification: Target cloud configuration provisions only a single US region (us-central1). If this entire region suffers an outage, the platform lacks a secondary US region to restore service while maintaining strict US data residency.
sensitivity_points: Absence of secondary regional cloud infrastructure within US legal boundaries
tradeoffs: Single-region cloud operational simplicity versus disaster recovery availability during complete regional outage

MOD-01.justification: The Integration Service decouples routing from external protocols using Spring Integration. Adding a new EU national standard requires either updating or adding a country adapter without impacting core telehealth services.
sensitivity_points: Modularity and pluggability of regional integration adapter contracts
tradeoffs: Centralized integration service complexity versus domain service isolation from national standards

MOD-02.justification: The Model Registry Client pulls version-pinned models from GCP Artifact Registry, while the Audit & Traceability Logger links every prediction and input to the active model version inside immutable Cloud Storage.
sensitivity_points: Strict version pinning and immutability of audit logs in compliance storage
tradeoffs: Deployment friction of version-pinned models versus strict MDR compliance traceability

SEC-01.justification: Cross-border isolation is enforced via VPC Service Controls, Istio egress controls, an External Consent Validator, and the Consent & Privacy Manager, denying cross-region requests lacking valid cryptographic consent tokens and logging all attempts.
sensitivity_points: Zero-trust cross-cluster validation and cryptographically signed consent verification
tradeoffs: Granular cross-region consent policy enforcement latency versus strict data sovereignty compliance

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates are processed by the Consent & Privacy Manager. While tokens embed consent to avoid synchronous lookups, the 24-hour window easily allows token expiry or revocation propagation, with operations logged in the audit trail.
sensitivity_points: JWT token maximum lifespan versus revocation propagation delay
tradeoffs: Stateless token validation efficiency versus instant global revocation of withdrawn consent
